title: Transferable Entitlement Windows: Team-level Borrowing, Auto-repair & Billing Audit Trails
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise customers running multiple product teams want the ability to borrow unused quota across team buckets within a defined window, see transparent invoice impact, and automatically repair allocation errors without manual ops intervention. Current behavior: entitlements are siloed per plan+route and overages generate immediate invoices and manual dispute tickets. This PRD defines transferable entitlement windows (TEW): a timebound, auditable mechanism to allow temporary borrowing across team-level buckets with automatic reconciliation and optional refund/credit routing.
goals: Allow customers to configure transferable windows that enable team-level borrowing of entitlement credits for a configurable timebox (e.g., 1–72 hours)
Ensure all borrowing activity produces immutable audit trails usable for billing reconciliation and customer-facing invoice line-items
Automate reconciliation and auto-repair flows that close the window and either reassign consumption back to original buckets, apply credits, or trigger defined overage policies
Surface real-time cost impact and provide invoice preview before end-of-window reconciliation
Keep latency, rate-limit, and SLO surface unaffected by entitlement routing decisions
non_goals: Create new pricing tiers or change base per-token prices
Replace existing dedicated capacity reservation model
Provide cross-organization (multi-tenant) entitlement borrowing outside a single customer account
scope: In scope: API + Console controls for creating TEWs, per-caller routing logic to prefer borrowed credits while preserving per-route priority, billing export updates with additional line-items and audit IDs, reconciliation worker to close windows and run auto-repair, customer invoice preview UI. Out of scope: deep refunds via payment gateway (we will surface credit adjustments; finance team will convert to refunds as manual step).
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create a TEW via API and Console with configurable duration (1h, 6h, 24h, 72h) and priority order of participating buckets
During an active TEW, requests that would otherwise overage are routed to eligible borrowed credits automatically without increased latency beyond 20ms median overhead

Every unit consumed from a borrowed bucket is recorded with a unique audit_id, original_bucket_id, consuming_bucket_id, timestamp, request_id, and reconciliation_flag and is included in the billing export CSV/JSON

At TEW end, reconciliation worker runs in <5m and: (a) attempts to attribute consumption back to original buckets where capacity exists, (b) applies credits per configured rules, or (c) applies standard overage charge if auto-repair disabled
Console invoice preview displays projected credit moves and estimated monetary impact with a confidence note for pending auto-repair within 1 minute of TEW creation and again at TEW end
Admin users can opt-in to automatic crediting or manual review flows; opting for manual review prevents auto-charge application until Finance approval
Billing exports and invoice line-items include TEW audit_id so customers and support can correlate consumption traces to invoice adjustments
Unit and integration tests cover routing logic, audit record generation, reconciliation job, and console preview UI; no regression in existing quota enforcement tests
Performance gate: reconciliation worker must handle top 95th percentile customer with up to 100M tokens consumed during TEW within a 15-minute reconciliation window in staging
success_metrics: Reduction in billing disputes related to team bucket overages by 45% in first 90 days
>70% of enterprise customers with multiple team buckets enable TEW in 30 days of GA via Console
Median additional latency from TEW routing <20ms across 95% of requests
Rate of failed auto-repairs <2% in steady-state over first quarter after launch
implementation_notes: Add TEW table to entitlement service with columns: audit_id (UUID), customer_id, window_start, window_end, participant_bucket_ids (list), priority_order (list), auto_repair_mode (enum), created_by
Add lightweight per-request check in routing layer that queries in-memory TEW index keyed by customer and route to avoid hops to DB under normal load
Reconciliation worker must be idempotent and emit a reconciliation_event per window. Events written to billing-export topic consumed by billing pipeline
Console: new TEW creation flow with guardrails, and invoice preview uses staging pricing engine query to estimate impact
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal Redwood tenancy only, enable TEW via feature flag; monitor audit logs and reconciliation job behavior
Phase 1 (private beta): invite 5 enterprise customers with multi-team orgs, collect feedback and billing edge cases
Phase 2 (GA): enable self-serve in Console; default TEW disabled for new accounts, must be explicitly enabled by account admin
Backout plan: if >5% of reconciliations fail or increase disputes by 10% in 7-day window, auto-disable TEW and surface rollforward instructions to affected customers
test_cases: Create TEW with two buckets A,B; consume from B beyond B's quota and assert charges are applied to A during window; after window assert reconciliation moves consumption back if A has capacity
Create TEW with auto_repair disabled; confirm invoice shows overage for consuming bucket and no credits applied
Simulate high-throughput consumption (100M tokens) in staging and measure reconciliation time and memory usage of worker
Verify audit_id is present in billing export and matches per-request logs for tracing
UI: create TEW from Console and validate invoice preview numbers match API-estimated projection
open_questions: Should minimum TEW duration be enforced (e.g., 1 hour)? Current recommendation: yes to avoid thrash
What controls should be available to partners vs. account-admins? Consider RBAC scope for enabling TEW per-team
Should TEW credits be allowed to borrow from shared enterprise pool or only team-specific buckets? Recommendation: initially only team buckets to minimize cross-org accounting complexity
How should refunds vs. credits be surfaced in invoices to avoid double-counting when Finance converts credits to refunds?
decisions: Initial scope limited to intra-account team buckets (no cross-account transfers)
Audit_id required for every borrowed token record
stakeholders: Eng: Lena Park (owner), Miguel Santos (routing), Priya Shah (billing pipeline)
notes: We should coordinate with Finance on export schema changes early. Feature introduces additional billing complexity; recommend a 6-week private beta with customers who have dedicated solutions contact. Track disputes and SLO impacts as part of the launch dashboard.
